page: Middleware processes requests before/after handler in Hono. Handler returns Response (one per request). Middleware awaits next() to pass to next middleware or returns Response to early-exit. Registration: app.use(), app.HTTP_METHOD() for path and method specification. Built-in middleware: poweredBy(), logger(), basicAuth(). Execution order: first-registered middleware executes before next(), last-registered after. Error handling: exceptions caught by app.onError() or converted to 500. Custom middleware using inline handlers or createMiddleware() from hono/factory. Response modification after next. Context access and extension via c.set() and c.var. Type inference across chained middleware accumulates Variables types. Third-party middleware available for complex features. Questions: How do middleware and handlers differ? What's the execution order? How do I create custom middleware? Can I modify responses in middleware? How do I extend context type-safely? How do I handle errors in middleware?

sections.manifest: Handler returns Response, one per request. Middleware awaits next() and returns nothing (or returns Response to exit early). Registration methods: app.use() for all methods/paths, app.use('/path/*', middleware) for path match, app.post(path, middleware) for method/path. Execution: registered middleware processes before handler, then after. Early-exit: if middleware/handler returns Response, stops processing. Example chain: logger() -> cors() -> basicAuth() -> handler. Questions: What's the difference between middleware and handlers? How do I register middleware? What happens with early-exit?

Execution order by registration sequence. First middleware's before-next code executes first, after-next executes last (LIFO for after-next). Nested execution pattern: middleware 1 start -> middleware 2 start -> middleware 3 start -> handler -> middleware 3 end -> middleware 2 end -> middleware 1 end. Error handling: exceptions caught by Hono, passed to app.onError() or converted to 500 response. No need to wrap next() in try/catch. next() never throws. Questions: What's the execution order? How is error handling done? Do I need try/catch around next()?

Built-in middleware examples: poweredBy() adds header, logger() logs requests, basicAuth() for authentication. Imports: from 'hono/powered-by', 'hono/logger', 'hono/basic-auth'. basicAuth options: username, password parameters. Deno caveat: version mismatch between Hono and middleware causes bugs. Example: upgradeWebSocket from different version fails. Questions: What built-in middleware exists? How do I use basicAuth? What's the Deno version warning about?

Custom middleware inline in app.use(). Signature: app.use(async (c, next) => {...}). Logger example: logs [METHOD] URL. Header modification: await next(), then c.header('name', 'value'). Reusability: extract to separate file using createMiddleware() from hono/factory. Syntax: const logger = createMiddleware(async (c, next) => {...}). Type generics: createMiddleware<{Bindings: Type}>. Response modification: c.res = new Response('New'). Context in middleware arguments: use c.env.VARIABLE. Extend context: c.set('name', value), typed with Variables generic. Type inference across chain: each .use() returns Hono with merged Variables type. Third-party middleware: GraphQL, Sentry, Firebase Auth, etc. Reference: /docs/middleware/third-party. Questions: How do I write inline middleware? How do I make middleware reusable? How do I extend context type-safely? How do I chain middleware with types? What third-party middleware is available?

Context access inside middleware arguments. Direct parameter in app.use(): app.use('*', async (c, next) => {...}). Access c.env for environment variables. Example: cors({ origin: c.env.CORS_ORIGIN }). Extend context with c.set() inside middleware. Type-safe extension using Variables generic in createMiddleware. Access in handlers via c.var.name. Typed example: echoMiddleware sets c.set('echo', function), handler uses c.var.echo(). Questions: How do I access context in middleware? How do I use environment variables? How do I extend context?

Third-party middleware extends functionality beyond built-in. Examples: GraphQL Server, Sentry, Firebase Auth, and others. Depends on external modules for complex applications. Link: /docs/middleware/third-party for full list and documentation. Questions: What third-party middleware is available? How do I use third-party middleware?
